stem: What is the least number of whole working days the cartographer needs to digitize all 100 sheets?
stimulus: A cartographer is digitizing a collection of 100 paper survey map sheets. Working at a constant rate, she completes 1 sheet every 40 minutes. She works 6 hours per day and only on whole working days.
explanation: Put the rate into the units the question needs. 6 hours per day × 60 minutes per hour = 360 minutes per day. At 1 sheet per 40 minutes, that is 360 ÷ 40 = 9 sheets per day. The number of days is the total divided by the rate: 100 sheets ÷ 9 sheets per day ≈ 11.11 days. After 11 days she has finished only 99 sheets, so she needs a 12th day. Here you have to round up, because 11 days leaves the job unfinished.

common_errors.why: Computes 100 ÷ 9 ≈ 11.11 and rounds down. That leaves 1 sheet undone.
Stops at 100 ÷ 9 and does not turn it into a whole number of working days.
Computes 100 × 40 = 4000 minutes, then ÷ 60 ≈ 66.67 hours, and gives the total hours instead of days.
Reads '1 sheet every 40 minutes' as 40 sheets per hour. That gives 240 sheets per day, so 100 ÷ 240 rounds up to 1 day.

stem: What is the maximum number of complete hours of continuous recording the memory card can hold?
stimulus: A field seismometer takes 40 ground-motion readings per second, and it stores each reading as 3 bytes of data. It saves the readings to a memory card with a capacity of 36 megabytes, where 1 megabyte = 1,000,000 bytes. The card starts empty.
explanation: Build the rate with units: 40 readings/second × 3 bytes/reading × 3600 seconds/hour = 432,000 bytes per hour. The card holds 36 × 1,000,000 = 36,000,000 bytes. Hours = total ÷ rate = 36,000,000 ÷ 432,000 ≈ 83.33 hours. The question asks for complete hours the card can hold, so round down to 83. An 84th full hour would need more space than the card has.

common_errors.why: Rounds 83.33 up. The card fills partway through the 84th hour, so that hour is not complete.
Gives the unrounded quotient and ignores 'complete hours'.
Converts seconds to hours with ×60 instead of ×3600: 40 × 3 × 60 = 7200 bytes per hour, and 36,000,000 ÷ 7200 = 5000.
Computes 36,000,000 ÷ 120 bytes per second = 300,000 seconds and does not convert to hours.

stem: How many more seconds does Storyteller Q take to tell the tale than Storyteller P?
stimulus: A folklore studies team records two storytellers performing the same traditional tale, which is 5,400 words long. Storyteller P speaks at a constant rate of 150 words per minute. Storyteller Q speaks at a constant rate of 120 words per minute.
explanation: Time = words ÷ rate. P takes 5400 words ÷ 150 words/minute = 36 minutes. Q takes 5400 ÷ 120 = 45 minutes. The difference is 45 − 36 = 9 minutes. The question asks for seconds: 9 minutes × 60 seconds/minute = 540 seconds.

common_errors.why: Finds the difference in minutes and does not convert to seconds.
Converts Storyteller Q's total time (45 minutes = 2700 seconds) and stops before taking the difference.
Gives Storyteller P's total time in seconds (36 × 60) instead of the difference.
Divides the words by the difference in rates, 5400 ÷ (150 − 120) = 180, which is not the difference in times.

stem: How many euros does the worker's family receive?
stimulus: A seasonal farm worker earns $18 per hour and works 35 hours per week for 6 weeks. At the end of the season, the worker sends all of these earnings to family abroad through a transfer service. The service converts dollars to euros at a rate of 1 euro = 1.20 dollars, then deducts a flat fee of 45 euros. There are no other deductions.
explanation: Total earnings = $18/hour × 35 hours/week × 6 weeks = $3780. To convert, multiply by (1 euro / 1.20 dollars) so the dollars cancel: 3780 ÷ 1.20 = 3150 euros. Then take off the fee: 3150 − 45 = 3105 euros. Check the units on the conversion. Multiplying by 1.20 would leave dollars²/euro, which tells you the setup is wrong.

common_errors.why: Converts to euros correctly but forgets to subtract the 45-euro fee.
Multiplies by 1.20 instead of dividing: 3780 × 1.20 = 4536, then 4536 − 45 = 4491.
Subtracts the fee from the dollar total (3780 − 45) and never converts to euros.
Gives total earnings in dollars, before the conversion and the fee.
